propositions: Phase 3 remediation proposals lack validation checks despite Phase 2 findings being scored, allowing unreachable harms and reversals of recorded decisions to reach human approval unflagged.
Two blind proposers reading identical evidence in Phase 3 measure prompt stability rather than proposal correctness, creating a convergence-without-validity gap.
Adding harm_reachable as a fifth validity sub-question with reachability-triggered HARDENING reclassification closes the harm-validation gap without modifying schema or test fixtures.

Implementing prior_decision as a deterministic four-value query on commit/ADR/ticket records with -0.10 validity penalty for reversals of explicit_justified decisions without evidence_changed citation closes the reversal-validation gap.

Asymmetrizing the Phase 3 proposers (OSS research vs. project record) and replacing tiebreak veto with targeted divergence research (bucket-weighted community adoption vs. project adoption record) surfaces unresolved conflict as no-consensus items for human adjudication.

Surfacing prior_decision record, evidence_changed, HARDENING flag, and no-consensus both-positions (not winner) in Phase 4 approval completes the audit trail without adding new plan-item schema fields.
